name: Question 20
problem:
A course grade is calculated by adding the results of a written test, oral test, and colloquium, contributing $50%$, $30%,$ and $20%,$ respectively to the final grade. 

The written test results are normally distributed with a mean of $64$ and a standard deviation of $8.$ The oral test results are normally distributed with a mean of $50$ and a standard deviation of $10$, while the results of the colloquium are normally distributed with a mean of $60$ and a standard deviation of $10.$ Find the probability that a randomly selected student achieves a grade greater than $70.$ You may assume that the scores on each test are independent.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.9\,$ | $\,0.9713\,$ | $\,0.9719\,$ | $\,0.9726\,$ | $\,0.9732\,$ | $\,0.9738\,$ |
| $\,2.0\,$ | $\,0.9772\,$ | $\,0.9778\,$ | $\,0.9783\,$ | $\,0.9788\,$ | $\,0.9793\,$ |
| $\,2.1\,$ | $\,0.9821\,$ | $\,0.9826\,$ | $\,0.9830\,$ | $\,0.9834\,$ | $\,0.9838\,$ |
worked_solution:
Let ${X}_{1}$, ${X}_{2},$ and ${X}_{3}$ denote the written test, oral test, and colloquium results, respectively. Then, we have

$$
{X}_{1}∼N(64,{8}^{2}),\,{X}_{2}∼N(50,{10}^{2}),\,{X}_{3}∼N(60,{10}^{2}).
$$

Let the random variable $Y$ denote the final grade of a randomly selected student. Since the written, oral, and colloquium contribute $50%$, $30%,$ and $20%$, respectively, to the final grade, we have

$$
Y=0.5{X}_{1}+0.3{X}_{2}+0.2{X}_{3}.
$$

The random variable $Y$ is normally distributed, where

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & =0.5\cdot 64+0.3\cdot 50+0.2\cdot 60 \\  & =59, \\ \text{Var}[Y] & =(0.5)^{2}\cdot {8}^{2}+(0.3)^{2}\cdot {10}^{2}+(0.2)^{2}\cdot {10}^{2} \\  & =0.25\cdot 64+0.09\cdot 10+0.04\cdot 100 \\  & =29.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}Y & ∼N(59,29).\end{aligned}
$$

In order to find $P(Y>70),$ we convert $Y$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y>70) & =P(Z>\frac{70-59}{\sqrt{29}}) \\  & ≈P(Z>2.04) \\  & =1-P(Z<2.04) \\  & =1-Φ(2.04)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(2.04)≈0.9793.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y>70) & ≈1-Φ(2.04) \\  & ≈1-0.9793 \\  & =0.0207.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Let X1, X2, and X3 denote the written test, oral test, and colloquium results, respectively. Then, we have

X1∼N(64,82),X2∼N(50,102),X3∼N(60,102).

Let the random variable Y denote the final grade of a randomly selected student. Since the written, oral, and colloquium contribute 50%, 30%, and 20%, respectively, to the final grade, we have

Y=0.5X1+0.3X2+0.2X3.

The random variable Y is normally distributed, where

E[Y]=0.5⋅64+0.3⋅50+0.2⋅60=59,Var[Y]=(0.5)2⋅82+(0.3)2⋅102+(0.2)2⋅102=0.25⋅64+0.09⋅10+0.04⋅100=29.

Therefore, Y∼N(59,29).

In order to find P(Y>70), we convert Y to a standard normal random variable by z-scoring: P(Y>70)=P(Z>70−5929)≈P(Z>2.04)=1−P(Z<2.04)=1−Φ(2.04)

Using the z-table, we see that

Φ(2.04)≈0.9793.

Therefore,

P(Y>70)≈1−Φ(2.04)≈1−0.9793=0.0207.
